broadcast independence has been introduced by Fiala, Golovach, Kratochvíl, and Krnc, and it has been proved that it is NP-hard to compute the broadcast independence number of a graph, even when restricted to bipartite graphs, chordal graphs, or graphs of diameter at most $2$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computation of broadcast independence number of a graph is $\mathcal{NP}$-hard, but the computation of the maximum independent broadcast of a graph is polynomial-time solvable.
